title: Wiseman–Wilson Theorem for Complex Conics
statement: Let $P\subset\mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C})$ be a finite point set not contained in a conic. Must there be a conic determined by exactly five points of $P$ and containing no other point of $P$, as in the real Wiseman–Wilson theorem?
